title: Earn in-game royalties for other players playing the game
author: Rhuneark
selftext:
TL;DR: I made a game in Run where you're a Barista crafting unique drinks and earning royalties for other players playing the game. Check it out [here](https://w.run/rhuneark/the-grind).

THE GAME:

This is my game called The Grind. Basically you're a Barista who serves customers in a uniquely styled minigame...actually 2 different minigames. Then use those funds to buy supplies, which are ingredients, to craft your own drink. There's 3 slots to craft a drink, and with 50 ingredients currently, that's well over enough possibilities that most, or all, people who play will have there very own set of drinks within the first few minutes of playing. At 25 ingredients unlocked, it's 15,625 possibilities for reference, and each new ingredient unlocked only makes that go up significantly.

After you've crafted a drink, it earns royalties for every other player that plays the game and does their shifts. The more players, the more royalties that can be earned.

Craft a drink that performs well, and see your drink in the Building Top Drinks, maybe even reaching that #1 spot.

Everything in the main area, except for the title bar, is clickable too, from the buttons to the stuff at your workstation.

The video showcases a bit of the game, but it's honestly much better to play it and start crafting and doing things for yourself.

THE PROCESS:

I used Run's studio to basically vibecode most of what you see. It uses Anthropic I believe, maybe a few others too. My normal AI is Claude, so this worked out.

I also used ChatGPT to create the coffee station graphics.

Some of this was a pain, like making sure to use webp pictures so the game loads fast, and sizing based on percentages so it looks the same on desktop or phone, and making the AI craft me an edit mode so I can fine tune the placements and size of the graphics. Which, if you use Run, is a nice little trick to have, make sure if it's not producing the results you want, just tell it to make you an editor (obviously you'll have to make the prompt exactly what you want in the editor).

This didn't cost me a lot of credits anywhere honestly, so it's worked out pretty good. And some people have taken a liking to it, and have become frequent players, including myself 😆 

If you have any questions or ideas for it, let me know, otherwise if you want to check it out yourself, I'll paste the link.

https://w.run/rhuneark/the-grind
